summary.value: The Barbu de Boitsfort is a very small Belgian bantam with no large form. It takes its name from Watermael-Boitsfort, a district of Brussels. It is the youngest of the Belgian bearded bantams: breeders made it in the 1990s by crossing the Barbu de Watermael with the tailless Barbu de Grubbe. It was first shown at Bruges in 1997 and gained full Belgian recognition in 2001. The bird matches the Watermael in every way except one: it has no tail and no tail bone. Like its relatives it wears a full beard. Cocks weigh roughly 1.3 to 1.5 pounds and hens about 1 pound. Twenty-three color patterns are accepted in Europe. Its eggs are tiny, about one ounce each. Numbers are critically low, so it is mainly a bird for dedicated show breeders who want to help keep a rare line alive.
